meta.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
meta.subtitle: LeetCode 787 in one minute (pipeline smoke test)

lines.cap: 4 cities. Each flight is [from, to, price].
lines.say: Four cities. Each flight is from, to, price.

lines.cap: Start at src = 0, end at dst = 3.
lines.say: Start at city zero, end at city three.

lines.cap: k = 1: at most one stop on the way.
lines.say: k is one. At most one stop on the way.

lines.cap: 0 → 1 → 3 costs 700 with one stop. The answer is 700.
lines.say: Zero, one, three costs seven hundred with one stop. The answer is seven hundred.

lines.cap: Brute force tries every route: O(n^(k+1)) time.
lines.say: Brute force tries every route. Exponential time.

lines.cap: Question: what is simpler to count than stops?
lines.say: Question. What is simpler to count than stops?

lines.cap: Flights: at most k + 1 of them.
lines.say: Flights. At most k plus one of them.

lines.cap: Question: why read the old row while writing a new one?
lines.say: Question. Why read the old row while writing a new one?

lines.cap: So one round adds exactly one flight.
lines.say: So one round adds exactly one flight.
Depth first search with memo. Order k times E.

lines.cap: Bellman-Ford, k + 1 rounds: O(k·E) time, O(n) space.
lines.say: Bellman Ford with k plus one rounds. Order k times E time, order n space.
Dry run. Round zero reaches city one for one hundred. Round one reaches city three for seven hundred.

lines.cap: k stops → k + 1 rounds. Copy before you update.
lines.say: k stops means k plus one rounds. Copy before you update.
